title: Don't Starve
notes: Current rubric v6 has 100 equal native-evidence milestones: 50 survival-duration thresholds over five days and 50 resource, crafting, building and eating conditions. New model specs use high effort, one life and 10800 seconds, with live or three-second frozen execution as specified per Trial. Historical rubrics and Trial specifications remain unchanged; Jev keeps its declared budget. The existing undeveloped Wilson Long Day snapshot and difficulty exception are retained.
introduction: Don't Starve is a real-time survival and crafting game. A trial starts Wilson in an undeveloped first-day base-game world with DLC disabled and the official Long Day option, retaining a day/dusk/night cycle. This setting measures early continuous survival and ordinary resource, crafting, building and food progress rather than Adventure Mode completion. The exact life limit, charged-time cap, execution mode and rubric are supplied by the Trial and its separate pre-run interview. Surviving time is never pooled across deaths.
controls: W/A/S/D move. Space performs a nearby contextual action. F attacks a nearby target. Left click performs the primary action at the pointer. Right click performs the secondary action at the pointer. Pointer hover reveals native action labels, and dragging moves an object to a selected destination. Escape opens or closes menus, Tab toggles the map, Q/E rotate the camera, and Return confirms menu selections. Scroll changes zoom or scrolls the visible interface. These are ordinary input bindings, not a strategy. Number keys 1 through 9 and 0 activate the native action for items in inventory slots 1 through 10. The native mouse-operated crafting bar uses left clicks to toggle category tabs and pointer hover to select entries; clicking an entry or its native button activates it. The separate keyboard-operated crafting panel uses W/S to select a category, A/D to select an entry, and Space to activate the current selection. In that keyboard panel, a mouse click activates the current selection; moving the pointer does not select another entry.
